successors.name: Weimar Republic
successors.text: Prussia's territory in 1918, as the Free State of Prussia (proclaimed 9 November 1918) inside the Weimar Republic

ledger.x: 18 January 1701: Frederick crowns himself King in Prussia at Königsberg.
15 January 1701: the Gold Coast colony passes to the new kingdom and stays its dependency (a tint of the metropole).
1707: Neuchâtel passes to the King of Prussia.
1713: Prussia gets most of Spanish Upper Guelders, with its capital Geldern, by the Treaty of Utrecht.
1715 (bridging year): Prussia takes the Western Pomeranian ground south of the Peene in the Great Northern War.
21 January 1720: the occupation becomes a cession at the Treaty of Stockholm ('Prussia had been allowed to retain its conquest, including Stettin'); the gain follows.
21 January 1720: the Treaty of Stockholm gives Prussia Swedish Pomerania south of the Peene with Stettin.
1721: Prussia sells the colony.
1740: Prussia invades Silesia.
11 June 1742: the Treaty of Breslau ends the First Silesian War.
11 June 1742: Prussia gains Silesia.
1744: East Frisia falls to Prussia.
15 August 1744: Prussia invades Bohemia in the Second Silesian War; Prague falls on 16 September.
November 1744: Prussia is forced out of Bohemia and retreats into Upper Silesia; Dresden (25 December 1745) ended the Second Silesian War.
29 August 1756: Prussia invades Saxony.
1757: the Russians invade East Prussia.
1761: the Russians advance in Pomerania and eastern Brandenburg.
5 May 1762: Russia, under Peter III, makes peace with Prussia by the Treaty of Saint Petersburg and does not resume hostilities; the page does not date the Russian withdrawal.
5 May 1762: the Russian front in Pomerania and the Neumark closes with the Treaty of Saint Petersburg.
February 1763: the Treaty of Hubertusburg returns the powers to the status quo ante bellum and confirms Prussia's control of Silesia; the Prussian occupation of Saxony ends.
August 1772: the First Partition of Poland.
1791: Prussia buys Ansbach and Bayreuth.
23 January 1793: the Second Partition.
5 April 1795: the Peace of Basel gives France the Prussian lands on the left bank of the Rhine.
24 October 1795: the Third Partition.
April 1801: Prussia occupies Hanover.
October 1801: the Prussians leave; they 'stayed there until October', and the page adds that Prussia withdrew its troops after the Battle of Copenhagen (1801).
25 February 1803: the Final Recess of the Imperial Deputation compensates Prussia with secularised bishoprics, abbeys and imperial cities.
1805: Prussia occupies Hanover.
1806: Königsberg becomes a capital, after the defeat at Jena-Auerstedt of 14 October 1806.
15 February 1806: the Treaty of Paris, which superseded the Convention and 'incorporated its main terms', turns the occupation of Hanover into annexation.
15 February 1806: Prussia annexes Hanover.
February 1806: Ansbach goes to Bavaria (Treaty of Schönbrunn of 15 December 1805, made final by the Treaty of Paris of 15 February 1806).
February 1806: the Duchy of Cleves is joined with the Duchy of Berg to form the Grand Duchy of Berg and Cleves for Joachim Murat.
February 1806: the Principality of Neuchâtel is given by Napoleon to Marshal Louis-Alexandre Berthier.
October 1806: after the defeat at Jena-Auerstedt on 14 October 1806 the French overrun Prussia west of East Prussia.
9 July 1807: the Franco-Prussian Treaty of Tilsit ends the war (the Franco-Russian treaty is 7 July 1807).
9 July 1807: Prussia loses the polish partition lands. most Polish lands Prussia had held since the Second and Third Partitions became the 'Duchy of Warsaw'.
9 July 1807: the left bank of the Elbe goes to the newly created Kingdom of Westphalia.
9 July 1807: Białystok goes to Russia (the Belostok Oblast).
9 July 1807: Cottbus goes to Saxony.
July 1807: Danzig becomes a Free City.
1809: the court returns to Berlin.
1814: Neuchâtel returns to the King of Prussia.
9 June 1815: Prussia 'regained most of its pre-1806 territory'; the Final Act 'was signed on 9 June 1815'.
9 June 1815: three-fifths of Saxony to Prussia.
9 June 1815: Prussia receives Greater Poland, Kuyavia and the Chełmno Land, mostly in the Grand Duchy of Posen (most of the Duchy of Warsaw became that grand duchy).
9 June 1815: Gdańsk (Danzig) comes back to Prussia from the Free City.
9 June 1815: the Rhineland.
9 June 1815: the Province of Jülich-Cleves-Berg merges the former Prussian Guelders, the Principality of Moers and the Grand Duchy of Berg.
9 June 1815: the Duchy of Westphalia comes to Prussia from Hesse-Darmstadt, which received Rhenish Hesse in exchange; the Nassau lands lost by Orange-Nassau also went to Prussia.
9 June 1815: Swedish Pomerania 'was sold to Prussia', after Denmark had received it in January 1814 in return for Norway.
9 June 1815: Hanover gains 'formerly Prussian East Frisia'.
1848: Neuchâtel leaves Prussia; the page says it was 'under Prussian administration until 1848'.
1850: the Hohenzollern principalities 'were annexed by Prussia in 1850'.
1 February 1864: 'The war began on 1 February 1864, when Prussian and Austrian forces crossed the border into the Danish fief Schleswig'.
30 October 1864: the Treaty of Vienna; 'Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria'.
30 October 1864: the Treaty of Vienna puts Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg under Prussia and Austria together.
14 August 1865: the Gastein Convention ends the joint holding.
14 August 1865: under the Gastein Convention 'Prussia took over the administration of Schleswig', Austria administering Holstein.
September 1865: the King of Prussia takes Lauenburg as its duke, in personal union.
1866: Hesse-Darmstadt hands over Hesse-Homburg.
1866: Bavaria cedes Bad Orb, Gersfeld and the Kaulsdorf exclave.
23 August 1866: Schleswig-Holstein is annexed after being an Austro-Prussian condominium; the Peace of Prague.
23 August 1866: the Peace of Prague gives Prussia Schleswig-Holstein, annexed after having been an Austro-Prussian condominium; it became the Prussian Province of Schleswig-Holstein.
23 August 1866: Prussia annexes Hanover, one of four of Austria's former allies (with Hesse-Kassel, Nassau and Frankfurt).
23 August 1866: Prussia annexes Hesse-Kassel,.
23 August 1866: Prussia annexes Nassau.
23 August 1866: Prussia annexes the Free City of Frankfurt.
November 1918: the Kingdom of Prussia ends.

wars.name: Great Northern War (Prussia's part)
wars.outcome: Prussia kept its conquest: the Treaty of Stockholm (21 January 1720) gave it Western Pomerania south of the Peene with Stettin and the islands of Wolin and Usedom; Sweden kept the rest, which Denmark returned on 17 January 1721.

wars.name: First Silesian War
wars.outcome: Prussian victory: the Treaty of Breslau (11 June 1742) gave Prussia most of Silesia and the County of Glatz, 35,000 km2 and about a million subjects.

wars.name: Second Silesian War
wars.outcome: Prussia invaded Bohemia on 15 August 1744, took Prague on 16 September and fell back into Upper Silesia in November; the Treaty of Dresden (25 December 1745) left Silesia with Prussia, and Maria Theresa acknowledged Prussian control of Glatz there.

wars.name: Third Silesian War (Seven Years' War in Europe)
wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum: the Treaty of Hubertusburg (February 1763) confirmed Prussia's control of Silesia; Russia had made peace at Saint Petersburg on 5 May 1762.

wars.name: War of the First Coalition (Prussia's part)
wars.outcome: Prussia declared war in June 1792, invaded France with the Duke of Brunswick's army, retreated after Valmy (20 September 1792) and made the Peace of Basel on 5 April 1795, which recognised France's occupation of the left bank of the Rhine and cost Prussia its…

wars.name: War of the Fourth Coalition (Prussia's part)
wars.outcome: Prussia defeated at Jena-Auerstedt on 14 October 1806; the Treaties of Tilsit (7 and 9 July 1807) halved its area (5,700 to 2,800 square miles) and population (9.75 to no more than 4.5 million), with an indemnity set at 154.5 million francs on 9 March 1808…

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition (Prussia's part)
wars.outcome: Prussia changed sides (Treaty of Kalisch, 28 February 1813; declaration of war 13 March, received in Paris 16 March) and the war ended with the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814; the Prussian king entered Paris with the coalition armies on 31 March 1814.

wars.name: War of the Seventh Coalition (Prussia's part)
wars.outcome: The war lasted 20 March to 8 July 1815: Blücher's Prussians lost at Ligny (16 June) and arrived at Waterloo (18 June) 'with the aid of several Prussian corps'; the Second Treaty of Paris (20 November 1815) ended the Napoleonic Wars and France was reduced to…

wars.name: First Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum: Prussian troops crossed the Dannevirke into Schleswig on 19 April 1848 and took Fredericia on 2 May; Prussia signed the Armistice of Malmö on 26 August 1848 and made peace with Denmark by the Treaty of Berlin on 2 July 1850; the London…

wars.name: Second Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria (Treaty of Vienna, 30 October 1864); the Gastein Convention of 14 August 1865 gave Prussia the administration of Schleswig and Austria that of Holstein, and the Prussian king took…

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussian victory: armistice 22 July (preliminary peace at Nikolsburg 26 July), the Peace of Prague on 23 August 1866 dissolved the German Confederation, excluded Austria from German affairs and let Prussia annex Hanover, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau, Frankfurt and…

certainty.note: Treaty frontiers: Breslau 1742, Hubertusburg 1763, the partition treaties 1772, 1793, 1795.
The Tilsit rump and the French occupation (to 1812): the frontier is drawn from a reconstruction, not from a surveyed line.
The Final Act of 9 June 1815 and the Peace of Prague (1866) fix the frontiers; the Neuchâtel and Hohenzollern exclaves are approximate.
